ceiling_effect_caveat: C/C++ hits an exact 1.000 F1 for CodeBERT, GraphCodeBERT, AND Hybrid on the leakage-fixed data (test_samples=2578). Verified no remaining G2B/B2G or FLAW/FIX/POTENTIAL leakage in the training text (see leakage_fix.verification). Plausible explanation, not confirmed: the leakage fix's aggressive dedup shrank the test set to 2,578 samples, and Juliet's per-CWE vulnerability patterns are inherently templated/limited in diversity, so full fine-tuning of large pretrained code models can plausibly reach ceiling on held-out instances of the same limited pattern space. RF (0.9992) lands just under perfect on the identical data, consistent with a real ceiling effect rather than a new hidden leak. Recommend stating this explicitly as a limitation in the paper rather than presenting the 1.000s as unqualified.

multilang_java_csharp.note: All four models (RF, CodeBERT, GraphCodeBERT, Hybrid) trained and evaluated on leakage-fixed Java/C# data.
